review_output: {"summary":"No BLOCKER found. Lock order, same-request retries, legacy UTC time conversion, expiry capping and the final authorization re-check look correct. MAJOR: the first issuance permanently fixes the registration's visitorId, so later proven visitors are locked out. MINOR: the SQL never checks that the admission belongs to the submission; only the authorize callback does. NIT: database error codes map to misleading issuance errors.","findings":[{"file":"src/lib/live-metric-session.ts","area":"Registration binding / idempotency","severity":"MAJOR","issue":"The first issuance fixes the registration's visitorId (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`). A later request with a different proven visitorId is rejected for the whole version, even if the first one had none.","evidence":"INSERT ... visitorId ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; then rejects if `context.visitorId != null && context.visitorId !== registration.visitorId`. Row identities are immutable, so nothing can ever update it.","impact":"Issuing once without a visitor, or from a second device, permanently gets not_authorized for that submission/version. A re-verified submission (new verifiedAt) is locked out the same way.","recommended_fix":"Decide the rule explicitly. Either keep visitorId off the registration (separate association table) or allow a one-time null-to-value attach. Also give the not_authorized cause its own error.","required_test":"Issue with visitorId null, then with a proven visitorId. Also try two different proven visitorIds for the same submission/version. Assert the outcome matches the chosen policy.","confidence":0.75},{"file":"src/lib/live-metric-session.ts","area":"Scope binding","severity":"MINOR","issue":"The sources query joins admission `a` only on live and vendor. Nothing in SQL checks that the admission belongs to `identity.submissionId`, so only the authorize callback enforces it.","evidence":"`JOIN \"LiveViewerSession\" a ON a.\"liveId\"=l.id AND a.\"vendorId\"=l.\"vendorId\"`, with no condition linking a to f. The session row then stores registrationId and admissionSessionId together.","impact":"If the authorizer ever pairs tokens loosely, one viewer's admission plus another viewer's registration could produce a session. That would put metrics under the wrong attribution with no database-side backstop.","recommended_fix":"Add `a.\"submissionId\"=f.id` (or the actual linking column) to the join. Optionally add a database guard requiring the session's admission and registration to share a submission.","required_test":"Use a stub authorizer that returns a valid admissionId and a different verified submissionId on the same live. Assert not_authorized and that no session or registration row is inserted.","confidence":0.6},{"file":"src/lib/live-metric-session.ts","area":"Error mapping","severity":"NIT","issue":"Database errors map to ingestion error names that don't fit issuance: a unique violation becomes `sequence_conflict`, and any 23514/23503 guard failure becomes `evidence_rejected`.","evidence":"In the `.catch`: `23505`/`P2002` → sequence_conflict; `23514`/`23503` → evidence_rejected. Issuance sends no sequences or evidence.","impact":"Callers and logs can't tell scope/guard rejections apart from real conflicts. A future HTTP route may return misleading status codes or retry advice.","recommended_fix":"Add issuance-specific mappings, such as issuance_conflict and not_authorized, or document the reuse. Log the constraint name on the server side only.","required_test":"Trigger the session expiry-versus-version check (23514) and a forced unique conflict. Assert the error codes and that no internal details reach the client.","confidence":0.7}]}
